t: You're standing by numbers one to four and their attached railings, a building in Camden. It was designed by John Nash, one of the great architects of Georgian and Regency London. Nash worked in the neoclassical and picturesque styles, and his designs were backed by the Prince Regent and by the property developer James Burton. He often worked with Burton's son, Decimus Burton. Look at the railings as well as the façade, since they belong to the same listed group. There's not much more I can say for certain, but the Nash connection is what makes it matter.
